exposure: Fetal position (occiput anterior, occiput transverse, occiput posterior)
outcome: Persistent occiput posterior (OP) position rate at birth
cohort: The study included 215 women with a single fetus in cephalic presentation, gestational age >37 weeks, and no previous or pre-labor cesarean section, from Moshi, Tanzania.
finding: The persistent occiput posterior (OP) position rate at birth was higher than previously reported (16.3%), and the operative intervention rate was nine times higher in women with the fetus in non-OA versus OA position in the second stage.
mod_finding: The operative delivery rate was significantly higher (58.3%) in the non-occiput anterior (OA) group compared to the OA group (6.4%) in the second stage of labor (p < 0.01).
cross-section timing: Fetal position was assessed at admission, in the first stage of labor, in the second stage of labor, and at birth.
